title: Front Brake Caliper Anchor Plate Removal and Installation
introduction:
The anchor plate is the sturdy frame around the brake pads. Getting it off means first removing the wheel, supporting the caliper and taking out the pads and their clips. This procedure covers the supplied 2.3L and 3.7L applications with the matching two-piston front caliper.

I use the illustration as a seating chart: blue identifies the anchor plate, magenta identifies its mounting bolts, and the bin symbol means those bolts do not get an encore. Keep the linked pad, wheel and lifting instructions with this procedure; they supply the access and finishing work that makes an anchor-plate job complete.

items.name: Have the installation supplies ready
items.detail: Have new anchor-plate mounting bolts, suitable torque equipment and a support hook for the caliper ready before dismantling. For wheel installation, use the anti-seize material identified in the Materials section of [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Select brake fluid from the Lubricants, Fluids, Sealers and Adhesives table in [Specifications](#/document/G1694687); the other brake-package rows do not change this job's applicability.

items.name: Prepare for the new-pad branch only if needed
items.detail: Replacing the anchor plate does not itself require new pads. If installing new pads, have a C-clamp and a worn brake pad available for piston compression. Install all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the pad kit, and use the kit's instruction sheet to determine lubricant application.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: WARNING: Before working around or underneath the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise the vehicle could be remotely started during service, causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear protection and check material safety information
items.detail: WARNING: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp or pointed parts. Failure to do so may cause serious personal injury. Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified chemicals or materials; improper use can present a health hazard and cause serious personal injury. If using solvents, keep them away from ignition sources because they can ignite or explode and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Control friction dust
items.detail: WARNING: Do not breathe brake dust or blow dust from friction components or storage containers with compressed air. Use government-approved dust-removal techniques. Dust created during friction-component repairs may present cancer and lung-disease hazards, irritate the skin, eyes and respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions or produce other chronic health effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury. Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183) before starting.

items.name: Use clean, specified brake fluid
items.detail: WARNING: Use only clean brake fluid meeting the manufacturer's specification, selected from [Specifications](#/document/G1694687). Never reuse drained fluid. These precautions help prevent system contamination, brake-component damage and serious personal injury. NOTICE: Immediately wash any brake-fluid spill on paintwork with cold water.

items.name: Apply the underhood precautions during the fluid check
items.detail: WARNING: Before working under the hood, inspect all cooling fans with the ignition OFF for damage, cracks or separation. A damaged fan can separate during operation; do not work under the hood with a damaged fan, and have it replaced with a new fan as necessary. Failure to follow this instruction may cause serious personal injury. Fans can run with the ignition off: disable them before working nearby to prevent personal injury. On vehicles equipped with engine auto start-stop, keep the ignition off when servicing or working close to rotating engine parts; automatic starting can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Use the specified lifting points
items.detail: Position the vehicle on a hoist with the transmission in NEUTRAL, as required by [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Use [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) to locate the lifting points, then identify the triangle stamped into the body or frame at each applicable point. WARNING: Lifting elsewhere can make the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Check hoist capacity and arm placement
items.detail: WARNING: Confirm that the hoist can support the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Position its arms at the locations shown in the lifting reference. Do not power the drive wheels with the engine unless every drive wheel is off the ground. Incorrect arm placement or powered drive wheels touching the ground can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Prevent contact damage
items.detail: NOTICE: Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering-linkage components. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and avoid damage to the axle or rear cover. Before using a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference. Do not apply jack pressure to either bumper; bumper-cover damage will occur.

items.name: If a jack is used
items.detail: WARNING: Use a jack with capacity adequate for the vehicle, cargo and modifications, on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Use the designated lifting points and support the raised vehicle with jack stands before going underneath. A jack can lower unexpectedly; relying on it alone can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death. NOTICE: The vehicle's supplied emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire; using it for this repair can damage the vehicle.

items.name: Remove the wheel and tire assembly
items.detail: After positioning and supporting the vehicle, remove the wheel nuts and take off the wheel and tire assembly using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). NOTICE: Never use heat to free a seized wheel nut; heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

items.name: Handle a damaged wheel safely
items.detail: WARNING: If the wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; failure to do so may cause serious personal injury. Do not weld or peen a wheel. A wheel needing those repairs must be replaced with a new wheel because wheel failure can cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable instructions in [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Support the caliper before removing the pads
items.detail: Remove the 2 brake-caliper guide-pin bolts, position the caliper aside and support it with a hook as illustrated in [Brake Pads - Vehicles With: 2-Piston Brake Caliper](#/document/G1693786). NOTICE: Do not let the caliper hang from its brake hose; doing so can damage the hose. These guide-pin bolts are separate from the anchor-plate mounting bolts.

items.name: Record pad and clip positions
items.detail: Note the component positions before removal. Remove the brake pads, then remove the top and bottom pad clips. The clips differ: the clip with the tab belongs at the top of the anchor plate. I check that tab before reassembly—it is the useful little landmark that keeps the clips from trading places.

items.name: Restore the clips, pads and caliper
items.detail: After installing the anchor plate with new mounting bolts, reverse the pad-removal sequence. Fit the tabbed clip at the top and the other clip at the bottom, restore the pads to their recorded positions, then refit the caliper. Tighten the caliper guide-pin bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm).

items.name: If installing new pads
items.detail: As part of reassembly, use a C-clamp with a worn brake pad to compress the caliper pistons into their bores so the caliper can fit over the new pads. Use all new hardware and the lubricant supplied in the pad kit, applying lubricant according to its instruction sheet. The illustration shows the worn pad distributing the clamp's push across the pistons.

items.name: Complete the brake-fluid check
items.detail: After brake reassembly, depress the brake pedal. Check the fluid level in the brake-fluid reservoir and top up as necessary with clean fluid selected from [Specifications](#/document/G1694687). This pedal application and fluid check remain required even when the pads were removed only to reach the anchor plate.

items.name: Clean the mounting faces
items.detail: WARNING: Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel's mounting surface and the mating hub or brake-disc mounting surface. Make sure any rotor-to-hub fasteners are secured and cannot interfere with wheel seating. Contamination or interference can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off while driving, causing loss of control, serious injury or death.

items.name: Keep anti-seize at the pilot interface
items.detail: Clean the wheel mounting surface, then apply a thin coat of the specified anti-seize only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot, as illustrated in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). NOTICE: Keep it off the wheel-to-disc/drum mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces; contact with those areas can damage components.

items.name: Seat the wheel and finish tightening
items.detail: Position the wheel and install its nuts finger tight initially. With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the nuts in the illustrated star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). This specification requires clean, dry stud and nut threads. NOTICE: Skipping the star/cross pattern can cause high brake-disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

items.name: Arrange the wheel-nut recheck
items.detail: WARNING: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; failure to retighten may cause serious injury to vehicle occupants.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they also contain details needed for installation.
edits.why: The mounting-bolt torque appears beside removal, so it needs to stay in view during reassembly.

edits.text:
Remove the brake pads before removing the anchor plate.
Refer to: Brake Pads - Vehicles With: 2-Piston Brake Caliper (206-03 Front Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Use the linked [brake-pad procedure](#/document/G1693786) for access: remove the wheel and tire, remove the caliper guide-pin bolts and support the caliper aside, record the pad positions, then remove the pads and the top and bottom clips. The preparation requirements above supply the handling precautions. I keep the clip positions clear because the tabbed clip must return to the top of the anchor plate.

edits.text:
Remove the 2 anchor-plate mounting bolts and take off the anchor plate. Discard the bolts; install new bolts during reassembly.
Installation torque: 85 lb.ft (115 Nm)
edits.why: The drawing identifies the anchor plate in blue and its mounting bolts in magenta. The discard symbol confirms that the removed bolts are not reused. The torque shown here applies when tightening the new bolts during installation.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal sequence: refit the anchor plate with new mounting bolts, then restore the brake-pad clips, pads, caliper, and wheel and tire. Tighten the new anchor-plate bolts to the installation torque given in the removal step.
edits.why: Reversing removal includes the linked pad and wheel work, with the new-pad branch used only when new pads are being fitted. The reassembly requirements explain clip orientation, piston compression when needed, caliper fastening, pedal application, fluid-level checking and wheel installation. Those finishing actions turn a refitted bracket into a completed brake assembly.
